MY_FINDING_1_the_coupling_term_is_taken_.what: qal/tankfed/coupling.py scans only ONE polarity of logic node (its gate loop skips gates by tf.is_hi). I reimplemented the committed free-vs-clamp differential from scratch and it reproduces the committed numbers EXACTLY (matched m2 o3_0 250.745 vs committed 248.997, rel 0.7%; uniform m6 o2_1 31.411 vs committed 31.411). On the UNSCANNED polarity of the SAME configuration and the SAME window I measure a +218.380 mV excursion on o3_1, a node intended LOW pushed UP -- the harmful direction.
MY_FINDING_1_the_coupling_term_is_taken_.so: the coupling term is wrong in BOTH configurations and in OPPOSITE directions: 7.0x too small for m6, 1.35x conservative for m2.
MY_FINDING_1_the_coupling_term_is_taken_.verdict_impact: banktank insensitive (57 -> 55 rows under my harshest scheme). chain3 unaffected in direction (still 0).

MY_FINDING_3_the_budget_DOUBLE_COUNTS_de.what: the criterion reads the ACTUAL signal against the ACTUAL receiver rail at the ACTUAL instant, on the committed transient. Held-rail droop is therefore already in that waveform, and so is any top-up coupling whose window precedes the commit instant. Adding them to the budget charges the row twice.
MY_FINDING_3_the_budget_DOUBLE_COUNTS_de.steelman_for_the_primary: for chain3 the top-up window (e.g. c_g100_topup bank2 [426.0,446.0] ps) falls AFTER the commit instant of link 1->2 (rail2 peaks near 420 ps), so for THAT link the step is genuinely absent from the reading and a budget term is justified. The term is defensible; its MAGNITUDE, imported from a foreign topology, is not.
MY_FINDING_3_the_budget_DOUBLE_COUNTS_de.measured_impact_chain3: rows passing functionally: 13 at NB=0, 11 at 3*sigma only, 10 at 3*sigma+droop, 7 at the primary's topup_m6, 0 at the primary's topup_worst. The whole 'chain3 changes nothing' headline is that one term.

The primary disclosed this; I confirm it, and I confirm the strict alternative is broken: scoring the last bank at its own rail peak fails EVERY iso-swing dv1200 free row at EVERY beat including T=300 (worst -68.13 mV), a row the committed VALUE check passes 32/32. The generous treatment is forced, not flattering.
D_THE_TWO_FAILURE_MODES_POLICED.MY_FINDING_5_worst_over_window_is_ILL_PO: I tested the stricter 'margin must hold throughout the receiving rail's charging window'. It passes ZERO rows in either dataset (worst window margin -194.7 mV chain3, -190.7 mV banktank). It cannot be right: a HIGH link is structurally below any threshold before its own rail has risen. So the primary's single-instant criterion is the correct choice, and the level.cir 33.3 mV worst-over-ramp margin cannot be promoted into a chain criterion. This check VINDICATES the primary.

F_CHAIN3_VERDICT_DOES_CHANGE._headline: THE PRIMARY'S PHASE-1 HEADLINE IS WRONG FOR chain3. 'chain3 carries no coupling measurement of its own' was true of the committed files but not of the circuit: the number is one deck away, and I ran it.
F_CHAIN3_VERDICT_DOES_CHANGE.the_experiment: I copied two chain3 topped-up decks into my own directory and changed EXACTLY FOUR LINES each -- the two top-up gate PWLs for banks 2 and 3 -- to park the top-up devices OFF while leaving them physically present and the whole resonant schedule byte-identical. That is qal/tankfed/coupling.py's own stated convention ('the same top-up devices PHYSICALLY PRESENT, parked off'). Decks: fcrit_skept/park_g100_topup.cir, park_g10_topup.cir.

G_PHASE2_FAIRNESS_THE_VERDICT_REVERSES._what_IS_fair: the BARS are genuinely identical on both sides -- I read both committed decks and both use 0.664485 V rise / 0.625839 V fall, and my own single-run deck reproduces every committed number: comparator 94.1745 -> 51.8985, 2 fF cell 57.1428 -> 32.9288, QAL settle 40.4171 -> 16.2030, pull-down peak 287.266 mV. The budget is the same 3*sigma on both sides. The DELVTO error is NOT repeated.
G_PHASE2_FAIRNESS_THE_VERDICT_REVERSES._what_is_NOT_fair: the criterion is applied to the identical BAR but not to the identical OBJECT. The QAL side is scored as a PIPELINE BEAT (pass/fail over every link at a fixed schedule). The CMOS side is scored as ONE GATE's rise time from an ideal 2 ps step. Those two have structurally different exposure to a bar change: in the single-gate measurement only the FAR END of the interval moves with the bar, so ~46% of the measured interval is tail and the bar change cuts it. In a pipeline both ends move together.
G_PHASE2_FAIRNESS_THE_VERDICT_REVERSES.THE_ARM_THE_PRIMARY_DID_NOT_BUILD: fcrit_skept/sk_chain.cir (depth 12, 2 fF/node) and sk_chain691.cir (depth 10, 6.91 fF/node -- iso-load with the committed comparator). Same cell, same supply, same 2 ps launch edge, same bars.
G_PHASE2_FAIRNESS_THE_VERDICT_REVERSES.THE_ANSWER_TO_THE_BRIEFS_QUESTION: YES, QAL gains more -- at the beat as well as at the level. QAL 1.3333x against a CMOS PIPELINE STAGE's 1.0989x (depth 8, the campaign's own committed sha_slice depth) and against a steady-state per-logic-level gain of 1.00000x. The primary's 'CMOS gains 1.8146x, more than QAL' compares a QAL pipeline against a CMOS single gate.

THE_RATIO_CORRECTED.so: the sign of the headline is set entirely by which CMOS object is in the denominator. The bar-invariant one (per-logic-level propagation) is the one a beat is made of.

G_PHASE2_FAIRNESS_THE_VERDICT_REVERSES.my_correction_is_CONSERVATIVE_against_QA: the CMOS chain I built has NO register tax, no clock, no setup/skew -- pure combinational propagation, the most CMOS-favourable pipeline analogue available. The QAL beat carries its whole resonant schedule. The conclusion flips anyway.
